candidates.rationale: EPS/BPS rebuilds return on equity from the two per-share numbers just reported, while $roe is a trailing aggregate ratio; when the rebuilt figure runs above the reported one, the screens and quality indices that rank on reported ROE are working from a stale denominator and have not yet bid the improvement into the price.

Book value per share only compounds organically out of retained earnings, so a fast growth rate in it means share issuance, capitalised cost or acquisition accounting; externally financed balance-sheet growth is systematically followed by weak returns because managers issue when their equity is dear.

The same accrual is far more suspicious at an asset-heavy, low-turnover firm, where it is likely capitalised spending that will never earn its cost of capital, than at an asset-light firm, where it is ordinary working-capital timing; scaling by turnover separates the two readings that the raw accrual conflates.

Capital structure decides which quality question actually binds: for a levered firm survival turns on whether reported earnings are cash, so accrual quality is the live risk, while for an unlevered firm the only question is whether the business earns a margin at all; applying the metric that matters in each regime beats applying one metric to both.

The quarterly change in earnings per share put on the firm's own equity base is an earnings innovation measured with no price input at all, so it captures post-revision drift directly from the report stamp rather than through a market reaction that has already partly discounted it.

In a name that is cheap on earnings, several days of trading well below its own open is dealer and index inventory being worked off rather than news, since the earnings anchor has not moved; the give-back is a liquidity concession that is paid back once the seller is done.

A wide-margin firm that printed its two-week low only days ago is being sold by someone with a deadline rather than repriced, because the operating cushion is unchanged; it is the recency of the low, not its depth, that distinguishes forced selling from information.

Book-to-price struck against a two-month average low is a valuation anchor that ignores recent price noise, and among genuinely cheap names a three-day volume burst marks the session the marginal seller clears, so cheapness plus a volume spike times the entry instead of warning against it.

Levered equity is a call option on the assets, so it is the security repriced first when funding conditions turn; short-horizon participation collapsing relative to the month is the market stepping away from exactly that claim, and the withdrawal predicts continued weakness among levered names while saying nothing about unlevered ones.

A high earnings yield only pays once the market stops marking the name down, so pairing the yield with where the stock sits in its own six-month range separates cheap-and-stabilising from cheap-and-still-deteriorating, which is the value trap that makes raw earnings yield unreliable.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. The three strongest accepts (5.59, 4.12, 3.87) all pair a fundamental level or 63-day delta with a short 5 to 21 day reversal or volatility term. Keep mining that pairing rather than fundamental against fundamental.
  2. Changing only the second multiplicative leg does not decorrelate: swapping a price scaler for a dollar-volume one plus CS_RANK for CS_ZSCORE still gave rho 0.845, and a window-only edit gave 0.984. Vary the fundamental leg instead.
  3. CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($field, w)) is exactly 4 nodes, so reusing any archived one is an automatic subtree rejection. Change the operator, not just the field or the window.
  4. The 21-day stochastic block (close less the 21-day low over the 21-day high-low range) is archived and matched twice this round at 5 and 9 nodes; prefixing it with a rank leg does not shrink the overlap. Long-horizon momentum over a dispersion denominator is likewise taken at rho 0.828.
  5. The coverage break is above 168 days, not at 126: DELAY($close, 252) failed at 0.872 even though it is a price field, alongside four 252-day fundamental normalisers (0.824-0.882) and a 126-day delta of a fundamental ratio (0.882). Price extrema at 126 days and a 168-day TS_RANK($close) both sat inside accepts, so treat 252 as the hard ceiling on any lookback and 126 as still safe on OHLC.
  6. Normalising a fundamental by a long-window TS statistic of itself went 0 for 4, all on coverage: TS_STD($roa,252), TS_STD($roe,252), TS_MEAN(ABS($accrual_gap),252) and TS_MAX($asset_turnover,252). Scale a fundamental with a price- or volume-derived series instead; every accept that scaled one did.
  7. Swapping $roa for $roe is not a decorrelating edit: the same spread times the same TS_CORR leg came back at rho 0.859 with only that field changed. Move to a different accounting dimension ($asset_turnover, $accrual_gap, $operating_margin) when the archived parent already uses one of the profitability pair.
  8. archive_subtree keys on the price/volume leg, so a fresh fundamental leg does not rescue a stale one: two proposals led by $operating_margin * $asset_turnover, a product that appears nowhere in the archive, still shared 5 nodes through their price legs. Spend the novelty budget on the price/volume subtree.
  9. Rearranging the operators around two legs does not move rho. MIN(fundamental rank, 1 - price rank) hit 0.806 against the product of the same pair; a fundamental divided by TS_STD($return,42) hit 0.817 against the same rank times a range ratio; and two simultaneous function swaps inside one price leg (TS_MIN to TS_MEAN in the numerator, TS_MEAN to TS_STD in the denominator) still held at 0.833. Change a field or a window, not the functions wrapped around them.
  10. Two legs beat three, on both gates. Bolting a third gated term onto an archived roe-minus-TS_CORR expression still scored rho 0.848, and the one accept whose price leg used three operators over two windows came in at fitness 1.366 while every two-leg accept scored 2.6 to 5.6.
  11. Fundamental acceleration is noise: a 63-day delta minus its own 63-day lag screened at |t| 0.68. The single 63-day TS_DELTA($roa) with no second differencing carried the round's second-best accept at 4.490.
  12. TS_RANK of a price series belongs on the multiplicative side, not in a rank spread. Subtracted from a fundamental rank at 42 days it screened at |t| 0.63; multiplied against a fundamental z-score at 168 days it scored 4.490.
